- Overestimate prices after recent spikes (especially when sentiment is negative or neutral) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward quickly.
- Underestimate prices during prolonged negative sentiment periods — model ignores bearish momentum, leading to lagged corrections.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., -1.0+), reduce forecasted mean by 2–5% relative to prior 7-day average to account for mean reversion.
- If sentiment turns sharply positive after a dip, model often overreacts — cap forecast increase to 3–5% above prior 7-day high to avoid overcorrection.
- For 30-day horizon, if last 3–5 days show strong downward momentum + negative sentiment, reduce forecast by 1–3% per day to reflect short-term volatility.
- When sentiment is flat (0.0–0.2), model tends to overfit recent trends — apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) to dampen noise.
- If sentiment is positive but recent price action is flat, model often overestimates upside — cap forecast at 1.5x prior 7-day high to avoid overbought bias.
